items.title: 1.6 Assessment of total uncertainty in the final result (final result mein total uncertainty ka andaza) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 1.6 with Examples 1.1 to 1.3 (PDF 12-14).

blocks.text: Agar calculation mein shamil har factor ki uncertainty maloom ho, to final result mein zyada se zyada possible (mumkin) uncertainty (error) yun nikalti hai:
1. For addition and subtraction (jama aur tafreeq ke liye)

Absolute uncertainties add ki jati hain (subtraction mein bhi add hoti hain, minus nahi hotin). Example: do positions (jagahon) x₁ = 15.4 ± 0.1 cm aur x₂ = 25.6 ± 0.1 cm ke darmiyan distance (faasla):
Aur do lengths ℓ₁ = 8.5 ± 0.1 cm aur ℓ₂ = 12.6 ± 0.1 cm ka sum (jor):
Colour printing (rangeen chhapai) sirf chaar colours, cyan, magenta, yellow aur black, se saare colours banati hai. Is kitab ke sab colours inhi chaar colours se bane hain.
blocks.title: For your information

blocks.text: 2. For multiplication and division (zarb aur taqseem ke liye)

Percentage uncertainties add ki jati hain. Example: ek conductor ki resistance R us par lagaye gaye potential difference V aur us mein behne wale current I se nikalti hai. R mein maximum (zyada se zyada) uncertainty yun nikalein:
Let (farz karein)
aur

blocks.text_alt: Percentage uncertainty in V = (0.1 V / 3.4 V) × 100 = 3%
Percentage uncertainty in I = (0.05 A / 0.68 A) × 100 = 7%

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab I ki percentage uncertainty ke fraction ke upar 0.5 A chhapti hai. Current ki absolute uncertainty 0.05 A hai (I = 0.68 ± 0.05 A), is liye sahi calculation (0.05 A / 0.68 A) × 100 ≈ 7% hai; kitab ka answer 7% bhi isi ke mutabiq hai.
Addition aur subtraction: absolute uncertainties add karein. Multiplication aur division: percentage uncertainties add karein. Power factor: power × percentage uncertainty.
blocks.title: Thumb Rule for Total Uncertainty

blocks.text: Is liye R ki total percentage uncertainty 3 + 7 = 10% hai.
R ki value:
10% of 5.0 = 0.5, is liye R = 5.0 ± 0.5 ohm likha jata hai. Uncertainty sirf estimate (andaza) hai, is liye use ek significant figure tak likhte hain.

blocks.caption: Travel time of light (roshni ke safar ka time) (For your information)

blocks.text: Kitab Moon (chand) se Earth tak roshni ka time 1 min 20 s likhti hai. Chand taqreeban 3.84 × 10⁸ m door hai aur roshni ki speed 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ hai, is liye time = (3.84 × 10⁸ m) / (3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) ≈ 1.3 s hai, ek minute se zyada nahi.
blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti

blocks.text: Pluto aur Earth ka distance badalta rehta hai, is liye Pluto se roshni aane ka time taqreeban 4 se 7 ghante ke darmiyan rehta hai; kitab ka 5 h 20 s ek rough estimate (mota andaza) hai.
blocks.title: Easy words mein

blocks.text: 3. For Power Factor (power factor ke liye)

Formula mein jis quantity par power lagi ho, us ki percentage uncertainty ko us power se multiply karte hain. Example: cylinder ka cross-sectional area A = πr² hai; yahan r par power 2 hai, is liye A ki percentage uncertainty = 2 × r ki percentage uncertainty. Power se multiply hone ki wajah se uncertainty barh jati hai, is liye aisi quantity ko zyada precise napna parta hai. Agar ek chhote sphere ka radius 0.01 cm least count wale Vernier Callipers se 1.25 cm napa jaye, to:

blocks.latex: \text{The radius } r \text{ is recorded as}\quad r = 1.25 \pm 0.01\ \text{cm}
blocks.text_alt: The radius r is recorded as r = 1.25 ± 0.01 cm

blocks.latex: \%\text{age uncertainty in radius } r \text{ is}\quad r = \frac{0.01}{1.25} \times 100 = 0.8\%
blocks.text_alt: %age uncertainty in radius r is r = (0.01 / 1.25) × 100 = 0.8%
Total percentage uncertainty in area A = 2 × 0.8 = 1.6%

blocks.text: Is liye result A = 4.91 ± 0.08 cm² likhna chahiye (1.6% of 4.906 ≈ 0.08).
Kitab yahan unit cm likhti hai. Area ka unit square centimetre hai, is liye sahi answer A = 4.91 ± 0.08 cm² hai.
blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
Example 1.1
blocks.problem: Ek metal (dhaat) ki sheet ki length 2.03 m, breadth (chaurai) 1.22 m aur thickness (motai) 0.95 cm hai. Sheet ka volume sahi significant figures tak nikalein.
steps: Given (diya gaya): ℓ = 2.03 m, b = 1.22 m, h = 0.95 cm = 0.95 × 10⁻² m
V = ℓ × b × h = 2.03 m × 1.22 m × 0.95 × 10⁻² m = 2.35277 × 10⁻² m³ (calculator ka answer)
Sab se kam significant figures 0.95 mein hain (do), is liye volume do significant figures tak likha jayega.

blocks.title: Example 1.2
blocks.problem: Lever balance se ek metal box (dabbe) ka mass 3.25 kg napa gaya. Beam balance se nape gaye 10.01 g aur 10.02 g ke do silver (chandi) ke coins us mein dale gaye. Ab box ka total mass sahi precision tak kya hai?
steps: Grams ko kg mein badlein: 10.01 g = 0.01001 kg, 10.02 g = 0.01002 kg
Sab se kam precise mass 3.25 kg hai (do decimal places), is liye sum (jama) ka answer bhi do decimal places tak.

blocks.title: Example 1.3
blocks.problem: 0.01 cm least count wale Vernier Callipers se ek metal cylinder ka diameter 1.25 cm aur length 3.35 cm napi gayi. Cylinder ka volume V aur us ki uncertainty nikalein.
steps: Length ki absolute uncertainty = 0.01 cm; percentage = (0.01 / 3.35) × 100 ≈ 0.3%
Diameter ki absolute uncertainty = 0.01 cm; percentage = (0.01 / 1.25) × 100 = 0.8%
V = πr²ℓ = π(d²/4)ℓ; d par power 2 hai, is liye V ki uncertainty = 2 × 0.8 + 0.3 = 1.9%

blocks.prompt: Pendulum ka time period T = 2.00 ± 0.01 s aur length ℓ = 99.5 ± 0.1 cm napi gayi. g = 4π²ℓ/T² se nikale gaye g mein percentage uncertainty kitni hogi?
blocks.explanation: ℓ ki percentage uncertainty = (0.1 / 99.5) × 100 ≈ 0.1%. T ki = (0.01 / 2.00) × 100 = 0.5%; T par power 2 hai, is liye us ka hissa 2 × 0.5 = 1.0%. Division mein percentage uncertainties add hoti hain: total ≈ 0.1 + 1.0 = 1.1% ≈ 1%. g = 4 × 9.87 × 0.995 / 4.00 ≈ 9.82 m s⁻², jo 9.8 ± 0.1 m s⁻² likha jayega.

blocks.text: Summary (khulasa)

items: Addition ya subtraction: absolute uncertainties add (x = 10.2 ± 0.2 cm).
Multiplication ya division: percentage uncertainties add (3% + 7% = 10%, R = 5.0 ± 0.5 ohm).
Power: percentage uncertainty × power (A = πr²: 2 × 0.8% = 1.6%, A = 4.91 ± 0.08 cm²).
Examples: V = 2.4 × 10⁻² m³; total mass 3.27 kg; cylinder V = (4.11 ± 0.08) cm³.
